parameters.content:
## Turn one video into native TikTok, Instagram and YouTube posts

### Who's it for
Creators, solo founders and small agencies who publish the same video to several networks and are tired of rewriting the caption three times — or of pasting the identical text everywhere and watching it underperform.

### What it does
You give it one idea and one video URL. PostWire's Smart Distribute writes a **native caption for each network** — the right length, hashtags, SEO and format per platform — and then publishes the video to every connected account in a single call. TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord and Reddit are supported.

### How to set up
1. Create a free PostWire account at https://postwire.io/dashboard.html (1 brand, 30 posts/month, no card) and connect your social accounts there with OAuth.
2. Copy your API key from the dashboard.
3. In n8n, create a **Header Auth** credential: name `Authorization`, value `Bearer pw_live_your_key`.
4. Select that credential on both HTTP Request nodes.
5. Edit the **Your idea, video and platforms** node with your own idea, video URL and networks.

### Requirements
- A PostWire API key (free tier works).
- A publicly reachable video URL (MP4). TikTok and YouTube reject text-only or photo posts.

### How to customize
- Change `platforms` to any mix of the supported networks.
- Swap the manual trigger for a Schedule, RSS or Google Sheets trigger to run it unattended.
- To queue a post for later instead of publishing now, call `POST /api/schedule` with a `run_at` timestamp.
- `brand_voice` is free text and steers every caption at once.

### 1. Your input
The only node you need to edit.

`video_url` must be a public MP4 link — TikTok and YouTube will not accept a photo or text-only post.

### 2. One idea → a caption per network
Smart Distribute returns a `drafts` object keyed by platform, each with the text (and title and tags for YouTube) written for that network's rules.

### 3. Publish everywhere at once
Returns one result per network, each with the post URL or the exact error.

TikTok starts as `SELF_ONLY` so your first test run stays private — change it to `PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE` when you are happy.
